stage: source-first questions frozen before candidate vocabulary
independence: Same author had read current ontology and prior packet. Questions preceded this dossier's candidate construction, but are not independent held-out tests. Fresh external probes still required.

questions.text: Whom do residents trust to give reliable wildfire warnings?
questions.source_motivation: directed reported trust, not demonstrated reliability

questions.text: Who has someone they can call on for evacuation help?
questions.source_motivation: support availability differs from delivered help

questions.text: Which affected groups were absent from the planning meeting?
Did residents cooperate in maintaining shared firebreaks?
Can people challenge the rules for accessing the community water supply?
Are people equally able to obtain help, even if they face the same hazard?
questions.source_motivation: access conditions differ from physical exposure

questions.text: Which organizations share responsibility for the watershed?
questions.source_motivation: polycentric arrangements not a single hierarchy

questions.text: Did warning messages pass between otherwise disconnected groups?
questions.source_motivation: communication ties are not trust ties

questions.text: How did confidence in local authorities change after the evacuation?
questions.source_motivation: reported trust change requires occurrence context; no assumed causation

questions.text: Were workers represented when recovery work conditions were negotiated?
When did a neighborhood mutual-aid group form?
Was a dispute settled, or did people merely stop attending?
questions.source_motivation: settlement and withdrawal have different interpretations

questions.text: Did assistance reach isolated residents as well as well-connected residents?
questions.source_motivation: network isolation and material need are separate

questions.text: Are people with low reported trust necessarily refusing to cooperate?
Can two groups agree on an action while disagreeing about its reasons?
